details:
* SECURITY UPDATE: CVE-2026-53795 - a destination directory swapped for a
     symlink during a transfer could redirect the receiver's renames, hard
     links and cross-filesystem copy fallback outside the destination.  Move
     to the complete rsync 3.1.3 security patch set (debian/patches/el8),
     which confines both sides of these operations, and drop the per-CVE
     patches it replaces.  The set also carries the bundled zlib fixes for
     CVE-2018-25032 and CVE-2022-37434.
   * Behaviour changes for a receiver outside a daemon chroot, as upstream:
     - a relative --temp-dir starting with "../" is refused (exit 23); give
       an absolute path instead
     - --partial-dir=../DIR keeps no partial file when a transfer is
       interrupted, and --inplace --backup-dir=../DIR leaves the backup
       without its attributes and exits 23
     - --keep-dirlinks no longer follows a directory symlink that points
       outside the destination
   * Fixed: --read-batch from a FIFO; on a daemon without "use chroot",
     --keep-dirlinks through in-tree directory symlinks and --files-from
     under a module subdirectory; --link-dest/--compare-dest with "../" in
     a "/./" module.
   * New options --sparse-block, --trust-sender, --insecure-links and
     --confine-root, and daemon parameters "insecure links" and
     "auth digest".
